evals.prompt: I want to build a small internal dashboard for support tickets. Interview me first, then write a short spec with stages, 5-minute tasks, and agent owners. Keep future ideas out of the actionable plan unless I approve them. Every task must be directly actionable and written in caveman style.
evals.expected_output: A concise Markdown spec created after clarification, with clear discovery and architecture decisions, checkbox stages, explicit agent ownership, caveman-style wording, and only concrete immediately executable tasks. Unapproved work stays outside the actionable plan.

evals.prompt: Help me plan a refactor of our billing service. I need you to ask questions until the migration risks and boundaries are clear, then turn it into a worker-ready spec file. Do not use vague tasks. Keep generated text caveman style.
evals.expected_output: A short refactor spec that clarifies service boundaries, risks, and staging, and breaks approved work into small caveman-style tasks with exact targets and fixed agent roles.

evals.prompt: I have an idea for a browser extension that saves snippets into project folders. Interview me and write a contract-style spec my workers can follow. Leave possible integrations in out-of-scope unless I explicitly approve them. Task text must be actionable, not vague, and stay caveman style.
evals.expected_output: A concise product spec with resolved ambiguities, a consistent section layout, explicit task ownership, caveman-style phrasing, and optional integrations kept out of the actionable checklist. Tasks name concrete outputs instead of vague intent.
